Subject: Question on geo-replication (EU primary / US DR) and DPA scope

Hi Rachel,

We're finalizing our disaster-recovery architecture and want to confirm how Redwood handles geo-replication for EU-based customers. Our architecture would write primary production data and logs to a EU region, but we want a cold DR copy in the US for resilience. A few questions before we move ahead:

- Does Redwood's managed runtime or any edge/cache components replicate request data or model KV caches outside the configured region by default?
- From a contract perspective: will we need SCCs + UK IDTA (UK Addendum) if we failover to US in a DR event?
- Are TIAs / DTIA signoffs required from our side for temporary emergency transfers?
- What evidence can you provide for procurement (SOC2, subprocessor map, retention policies) so our security team can sign off quickly?

I've attached a short DR plan (DR_plan_v2.pdf) so you can see expected failover cadence. Can we get a short write-up of the legal/controls path and any recommended clause language?

Thanks,
Martin Holt
Head of Infrastructure, Dr Systems
martin.holt@drsystems.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question on geo-replication (EU primary / US DR) and DPA scope

Hi Martin — thanks for the clear plan and questions. Short answers first, then proposed next steps: 

1) Runtime/replication behavior
- By default, customer data (requests, payloads) and logs are stored in the customer-selected region. Redwood's serving runtime will not persist production request payloads to a secondary region for normal serving.
- There are two places to watch: asynchronous backups (configurable) and cold DR replication. If you enable automatic cross-region backups for durability, those will be copied to the chosen DR target. Our edge nodes may cache transiently but do not write persistent copies outside region unless configured.

2) Contract/legal implications
- For transfers from EU -> US on a DR failover, standard SCCs are the baseline safeguard. If any data originates in the UK or you have processing tied to UK residency, the UK IDTA + UK Addendum will apply for UK->US transfers.
- TIAs/DTIAs: For emergency/temporary failover we typically document a short-term Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) / DTIA record that notes the exceptional nature and retention limits; in many enterprise deals we add an explicit emergency transfer clause to the DPA to avoid repeating approvals.

3) Recommended contract language and rollback path
- We can provide a one-paragraph emergency-transfer clause (see below) that describes allowed temporary failover, maximum retention in failover region, and the rollback cadence. Example (draft): 
  "In the event of a documented and material service disruption in Customer's primary region, Redwood may temporarily process and store necessary Customer Data in an alternate region for a period not to exceed 30 days unless otherwise agreed, after which Redwood will securely delete transferred data and restore processing to the primary region. Such temporary transfers shall be governed by the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) and, where applicable, the UK International Data Transfer Agreement (IDTA) and related UK Addendum. Redwood will provide Customer with notice of any such failover and a post-incident evidence package."

4) Evidence package
- We can provide: current SOC2 summary, most recent subprocessor map, retention and deletion playbook, and the DR rollback checklist. I attached a short SOC2 summary we usually share with procurement.

Next steps
- Kimberly and Laura (cc'd) will review contract wording and the rollback checklist and propose an internal sign-off path and a candidate DPA addendum.
- If helpful, we can do a 30-minute call to run through the DR plan and confirm the TTLs you propose for caches and backups.

Happy to align — propose Tue 7/6 10:00am CET or Wed 7/7 9:00am CET.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Thanks Rachel — quick internal notes and a proposed operational rollback checklist.

Operational considerations
- Make sure DR replication is an opt-in in the customer's control plane. Default should remain EU-only; enable US replication only if customer explicitly requests or signs the emergency-transfer clause.
- For services that use prefix/KV caches: set cache TTL <= 2 hours across edges in the failover config to avoid long-lived caches in alternate region.

Legal/contract template bits (to hand to Legal for DPA addendum)
- Add the emergency-transfer paragraph Rachel drafted.
- Add an obligation for Redwood to run a brief DTIA/TIA (1 page) that will be shared within 48 hours after failover and retained in the incident folder.
- Limit retention in failover region to no more than 30 days by default; delete snapshots used solely for DR within 7 days of restore unless otherwise agreed.

Attachment: data-transfer-rollback-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45 KB) — contains a checklist we can attach to the DPA as an operational exhibit.

I'll draft the DPA addendum with those bits; Laura, can you own the procurement evidence bundle (SOC2 pdf + subprocessor CSV + retention playbook)?

-kim
